summary: Sciences Po's Émile Boutmy Scholarship cuts tuition for its best students from outside the European Union: a full exemption or €9,500 off for the bachelor's, and €18,500 off in each of the two years of a master's. It covers tuition only, not living costs. Master's applicants have until 29 November 2026, and bachelor's applicants from foreign secondary schools until 13 January 2027.
meta_title: Émile Boutmy Scholarship 2027: Sciences Po tuition for non-EU
meta_description: Sciences Po's Émile Boutmy Scholarship: €18,500 off master's tuition a year, or up to full bachelor's tuition, for non-EU students entering in 2027.
covers: Bachelor's: a total exemption from tuition fees, or an exemption of €9,500.
Master's: €18,500 off tuition fees in each of the two years.
Sciences Po may recalculate the amount each year in line with tuition increases.
No living allowance, so rent and living costs in Paris are yours to cover. You can combine it with outside scholarships.
eligibility: Citizens of a country outside the European Union applying to Sciences Po for the first time.
Parents whose tax residence is outside the EU. Sciences Po looks at your parents' tax residence, not yours.
Admission to the undergraduate programme or a two-year master's.
Awarded on merit and on the profile each programme looks for.
how_to_apply: Apply to Sciences Po online and pay the application fee. Only complete files are considered.
Tick the Émile Boutmy Scholarship in the 'Financial information' section of the same application. You cannot ask for it after you submit, or after admission.
Master's: have your complete application in by 29 November 2026, the second and last Boutmy round. The first closed on 18 October 2026.
Bachelor's, applying from a foreign secondary school: apply by 13 January 2027. Results come in April.
watch_out: Not eligible: Swiss and Norwegian applicants, dual citizens with an EU nationality, one-year master's and PhD students, exchange students and Quebec master's candidates.
You lose the scholarship if you do not validate your academic year, or if you defer.
It cannot be combined with other Sciences Po scholarships.
documents: The Sciences Po online application, with the Émile Boutmy Scholarship ticked under 'Financial information'.
Language test results, if your programme asks for them.

faq.q: How much is the Émile Boutmy Scholarship?
faq.a: For the bachelor's, a full tuition exemption or €9,500 off; for a master's, €18,500 off tuition in each of the two years. It does not pay living costs.

faq.q: What is the Émile Boutmy deadline for 2027 entry?
faq.a: 29 November 2026 for master's applicants, the last Boutmy round, and 13 January 2027 for bachelor's applicants from foreign secondary schools.

faq.q: Who can get the Émile Boutmy Scholarship?
faq.a: First-time applicants from outside the European Union whose parents do not pay tax in the EU, once admitted to the bachelor's or a two-year master's.
